parole.significato: A spiced pork sausage typical of Catalan cuisine.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan botifarra.

parole.significato: An Italian helmet with a stalk-like projection on the top resembling a pear.
parole.testo: From Catalan cabasset, perhaps via French cabasset.

parole.significato: A human tower formed in festivals in Catalonia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan castell. Doublet of cashel, castellum, castle, and château.

parole.significato: A person who participates in building castells.
parole.testo: From Catalan casteller. By surface analysis, castell + -er. Piecewise doublet of castler.

parole.significato: A Catalan sweet made from almonds coated in caramel and powdered chocolate.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan catànies.

parole.significato: A Spanish white sparkling wine made using the méthode champenoise.
parole.testo: From Catalan cava (literally “wine cellar”).

parole.significato: A coin making up one hundredth of an Andorran diner (but, like the diner, not legal tender).
parole.testo: From Catalan cèntim. Doublet of centime, centimo, and santim.

parole.significato: A pastry typically made and consumed in the Catalan-speaking areas.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan coca. Doublet of cake.

parole.significato: Any of several forms of parade-like celebrations in Catalonia involving pyrotechnics in the middle of a crowd.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan correfoc (literally “run [through] fire”).

parole.significato: A commemorative currency of Andorra, not legal tender, divided into 100 centims.
parole.testo: From Catalan diner. Doublet of denar, denarius, denier, dinar, dinero, and dinheiro.

parole.significato: A type of pastry originating from Mallorca made from flour, water, sugar, eggs, dough and reduced pork lard named saïm.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan ensaïmada. Doublet of ensaymada.

parole.significato: A dish of marinaded shredded salt cod.
parole.testo: From Catalan esqueixada.

parole.significato: The Majorcan midwife toad (Alytes muletensis).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan ferreret.

parole.significato: A small piccolo-like wooden flute used to accompany the sardana.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan fluviol.

parole.significato: The interpunct, particularly as used in Catalan.
parole.testo: Calque of Catalan punt volat.

parole.significato: A type of thin salami from Catalonia made from pork.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan fuet, from French fouet.

parole.significato: Of, from, or relating to, Mallorca or its culture or people.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan mallorquí (“Mallorcan”).

parole.significato: A seaside marsh, used for agriculture
parole.testo: From Catalan marjal or Spanish marjal.

parole.significato: An irregular or partisan soldier in Catalonia.
parole.testo: Catalan miquelet, a diminutive of Michael. Supposedly named after a Miquel or Miquelot de Prades, a Catalan mercenary captain in the service of Cesare Borgia.

parole.significato: A member of the Mossos d'Esquadra.
parole.testo: From Catalan mosso (“police officer”), ellipsis of mosso d'esquadra, from Old Spanish mozo (“boy, lad”). Doublet of mozo.

parole.significato: A kind of megalithic chamber tomb, unique to the Balearic island of Minorca, with two vertical and two corbelled walls…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan naveta, diminutive of nau (“ship”).

parole.significato: A savory Valencian dish made of rice, cooked in a frying pan with vegetables and meat or shellfish.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan paella (“pot; pan”), from Old French paelle, from Latin patella (“plate, small pan”). Doublet of patella and possibly pail.

parole.significato: A thick red sauce based on nuts and tomatoes and used with seafood, originating in Catalonian cuisine
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan romesco.

parole.significato: A type of circle dance originating in Catalonia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan sardana.

parole.significato: A Catalan-speaking gentleman.
parole.testo: From Catalan senyor. Doublet of seigneur, seignior, senhor, senior, señor, signore, sir, and sire.

parole.significato: The sending sexual content without the consent of a party from which consent is required, comprehended as a type of cyb…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan sexpreading, equivalent to sex + spreading.

parole.significato: A spiced, cured pork sausage from the Balearic Islands.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan sobrassada, from Italian soprassata.

parole.significato: A kind of Bronze Age megalith found on the islands of Minorca and Mallorca.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan talaiot, from talaia (“watchtower”), of Arabic origin.

parole.significato: A kind of T-shaped stone monument, built by the Talaiotic culture, found on the Balearic island of Minorca.
parole.testo: From Catalan taula (“table”). Doublet of table.

parole.significato: A traditional Catalan Christmas character made by decorating a short log. It is “fed” with gifts each day from December…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan tió de Nadal, from tió (“log”) and Nadal (“Christmas”).

parole.significato: A Catalan dish of cabbage, potato and pork, resembling bubble and squeak.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan trinxat, the past participle of trinxar (“to slice”).

parole.significato: One of a strictly endogamous social group on the island of Mallorca, descendants of Mallorcan Jews who either converted…
parole.testo: From Catalan xueta.

parole.significato: A viennoiserie pastry filled with crema catalana, from Girona in Catalonia, Spain.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Catalan xuixo.

parole.significato: A sweet beverage variously made with rice, chufa or morro seeds (or, historically, barley), water, sugar, and cinnamon,…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish horchata, ultimately from Vulgar Latin *hordeata (“(drink, food) made of barley”), from hordeum (“barley”), either via Catalan/Valencian orxata (possibly via a Mozarabic source), or via Italian orzata. Doublet of orgeat (“almond syrup”) and orzo (“barley-shaped pasta”).
